segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After this Jesus went about in Galilee, for he did not want to go about in Judea, because the Judeans were seeking to kill him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now the festival of the Jews, the Festival of Booths, was near.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So his brothers said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Leave here and go to Judea, so that your disciples too may see the works you are doing.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: For no one does anything in secret while seeking to be in the public eye himself. If you are doing these things, show yourself to the world.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For not even his brothers believed in him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “My time is not yet here, but your time is always at hand.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The world cannot hate you, but it hates me, because I testify about it that its works are evil.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You go up to the festival. I am not going up to this festival, because my time has not yet been fulfilled.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Having said this, he himself stayed in Galilee.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But when his brothers had gone up to the festival, then he too went up, not openly but, as it were, in secret.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Jewish leaders were looking for him at the festival and saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Where is that man?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And there was much murmuring about him among the crowds. Some were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “He is a good man,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: but others were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “No, he is leading the crowd astray.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Yet no one spoke publicly about him, for fear of the Jewish leaders.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the festival was already half over, Jesus went up into the temple and began to teach.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Jews were amazed and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “How does this man have such learning, when he has never studied?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “My teaching is not mine, but belongs to the one who sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If anyone wants to do his will, that person will know about the teaching, whether it is from God or whether I speak on my own.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The one who speaks on his own seeks his own glory, but the one who seeks the glory of the one who sent him is true, and there is no wrongdoing in him.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Has not Moses given you the Law? Yet none of you keeps the Law. Why are you seeking to kill me?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The crowd answered,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You have a demon! Who is seeking to kill you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I did one work, and you are all amazed.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For this reason Moses has given you circumcision—not that it is from Moses, but from the patriarchs—and you circumcise a man on the Sabbath.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If a man receives circumcision on the Sabbath so that the Law of Moses may not be broken, are you angry with me because I made a whole man well on the Sabbath?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Do not judge by appearance, but judge with just judgment.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So some of the people of Jerusalem were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Is this not the man they are seeking to kill?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And look, he is speaking publicly, and they say nothing to him. Can it be that the rulers have really recognized that this man is the Messiah?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: But we know where this man is from; when the Messiah comes, no one knows where he is from.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus cried out as he was teaching in the temple,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You know me, and you know where I am from. Yet I have not come on my own; the one who sent me is true, and him you do not know.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I know him, because I am from him, and he sent me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they were seeking to seize him, yet no one laid a hand on him, because his hour had not yet come.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But many from the crowd believed in him, and they were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “When the Messiah comes, surely he will not do more signs than this man has done?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Pharisees heard the crowd murmuring these things about him, and the chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers to seize him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I am with you a little while longer, and then I am going to the one who sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You will look for me and will not find me, and where I am, you cannot come.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Jews said to one another,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Where does this man intend to go, that we will not find him? Surely he does not intend to go to the Dispersion among the Greeks and teach the Greeks?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: What is this saying of his, ‘You will look for me and will not find me, and where I am, you cannot come’?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: On the last day of the festival, the great day, Jesus stood and cried out,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Let anyone who is thirsty come to me and drink.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever believes in me, as the Scripture has said, ‘Rivers of living water will flow from within him.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now he said this about the Spirit, whom those who believed in him were going to receive; for as yet there was no Spirit, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So some from the crowd, when they heard these words, were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “This truly is the Prophet.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Others were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “This is the Messiah.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But some were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Surely the Messiah does not come from Galilee?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Has not the Scripture said that the Messiah comes from the offspring of David, and from Bethlehem, the village where David was?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So a division arose in the crowd because of him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Some of them wanted to seize him, but no one laid hands on him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the officers came to the chief priests and Pharisees, who said to them,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Why did you not bring him?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The officers answered,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Never has anyone spoken like this!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Pharisees answered them,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Surely you have not been led astray too?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Has any of the rulers believed in him, or any of the Pharisees?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: But this crowd that does not know the Law—they are accursed.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Nicodemus, who had come to him earlier and was one of them, said to them,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Surely our Law does not judge a person without first hearing from him and learning what he is doing?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Surely you are not from Galilee too? Search and see that no prophet arises from Galilee.”

notes.note: The Greek word names a people with a religion and a homeland, and no single English word covers it. Here the contrast is geographic, Judea as against Galilee, so “Judeans” is used. In verses 11 and 13, where the group is distinguished from the festival crowds and is feared by them, it is rendered “the Jewish leaders”; elsewhere in the chapter it is “the Jews.” Scholars are divided: some prefer “Judeans” throughout, while others object that this erases Jews from the New Testament.

This was the week-long autumn harvest festival, one of the three pilgrimage festivals, during which people lived in temporary shelters recalling Israel’s years in the wilderness (Leviticus 23:33–43). Later Jewish sources describe a daily water-pouring ceremony at the temple during the festival, which many scholars see as the setting for Jesus’ words about thirst and living water in verses 37–38.

Some early and important manuscripts read “I am not yet going up,” which removes the apparent conflict with verse 10, where Jesus does go. Many editors, including those of the Greek text translated here, judge “not” to be the earlier reading, since a copyist would more likely ease the difficulty than create it. The question remains disputed.

The Greek says literally that he “knows letters.” The point is not basic literacy but trained learning, here in the Scriptures and their interpretation. Such learning was normally acquired by studying under a recognized teacher, which Jesus had not done.

notes.traditional: Moses therefore gave unto you circumcision
notes.note: The Greek phrase can be attached to the end of verse 21 (“you are all amazed because of it”) or, as here and in the Greek edition followed, to the beginning of verse 22. Taken with verse 22, the thought is compressed: Moses gave circumcision, which overrides the Sabbath, and this sets the precedent for the healing Jesus goes on to defend.

Greek has one word-family where English has two: “righteous” and “just,” “righteousness” and “justice.” Because fair judging is the point here, “just” is used; the same Greek adjective is elsewhere rendered “righteous.”

The Greek word means the anointed king Israel expected, and in this chapter it is a title under debate, not a name. “Messiah” conveys that to a modern reader where “Christ” tends to sound like a surname. Several modern translations make the same choice in the Gospels and keep “Christ” where it functions as a name.

notes.phrase: no one knows where he is from
notes.note: One strand of Jewish expectation held that the Messiah would appear suddenly, his origins hidden until he was revealed. Others in the crowd hold a different expectation in verse 42, that he must come from Bethlehem. John lets both objections stand without comment, and Jesus answers by pointing to the one who sent him.

“The Dispersion” was the standard term for Jews living scattered outside the land of Israel, here those in Greek-speaking regions. “Greeks” in the second clause most likely means non-Jews. The speakers intend the suggestion as absurd.

The punctuation is disputed. The text follows the usual division, in which the rivers flow from within the believer. The words can also be divided as “Let anyone who is thirsty come to me, and let whoever believes in me drink,” in which case the Scripture may describe the water flowing from Jesus himself. No single Old Testament passage matches the quotation; passages such as Isaiah 58:11, Ezekiel 47:1–12 and Zechariah 14:8 are often suggested.

The Greek word means the belly or the womb, and it was also used for a person’s inner self. Older versions have “belly” and several modern ones “heart”; “from within him” gives the sense without suggesting anatomy that the saying does not intend.

notes.phrase: as yet there was no Spirit
notes.traditional: the Spirit had not yet been given
notes.note: The Greek says simply that the Spirit “was not yet.” Some manuscripts add “given,” and most translations supply it. John is not saying that the Spirit did not exist (compare 1:32–33); he means that the Spirit was not yet present with believers in the way that would follow once Jesus was glorified.

With the definite article this refers to a particular expected figure, the prophet like Moses promised in Deuteronomy 18:15–18. The crowd treats this figure as distinct from the Messiah, as in 1:20–21.

“Seed,” “offspring” and “descendants” all compete, and Paul’s argument in Galatians 3:16 depends on the singular, so one policy is needed across the New Testament.
Recurs for Jewish council members, civic magistrates and spiritual powers; “rulers,” “leaders” and “authorities” are all in use and should not vary at random.
Translations alternate between “deceive,” “lead astray” and “mislead” across the Gospels, the letters and Revelation, where the charge of deceiving the people is a recurring theme.
The word marks an appointed or opportune moment as against χρόνος, and translators differ over whether and how to signal the distinction (time, right time, season, opportunity).
